newsitem.title: UK: James Bond's lifestyle would kill him - magazine.
newsitem.headline: James Bond's lifestyle would kill him - magazine.

text.p: James Bond's compulsive womanising and heavy drinking would have killed off the famous hero of spy novels and films long ago, a health magazine said on Wednesday.
Bond's killer lifestyle would have left him impotent and crippled by liver disease, Men's Health said in a medical check-up on the late Ian Fleming's legendary character.
It calculated that Bond, who has continued starring in an apparently unending series of cinema spoofs long after Fleming wrote his last Bond novel, sleeps with 68 women a year.
Regular visits to brothels in exotic locations would lay him open to a gamut of sexually transmitted diseases because he never wears a condom.
The glamorous spy who likes his double martinis shaken not stirred was also castigated for his drinking habits.
"Bond's alcoholic consumption is incompatible with him still being alive," the magazine said.
Men's Health also estimated that Bond, who first hit the cinema screens almost 35 years ago in "Dr No," smokes 70 unfiltered black Turkish cigarettes a day.
"He is a sick man," it said.
The magazine concluded that the high-living epitome of glamour "appears to be abusing his licence to kill by killing himself".
